result:
I graded Riley's submission `s1` for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. The score is 2 correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | Riley said the model opens the booking system itself. The model only outputs a request naming the tool and its arguments. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the right safeguard against a stuck loop. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | Riley answered 1 call, saying the model "runs the 3 tools itself". The correct count is 4, because the program runs the tools between calls. |
| q5 | partial | "It sends it back to the model" is right, but Riley left out why, which is so the model can use the result to decide its next step or answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Riley was right that the model picks a tool from the names and descriptions it is given. Riley was wrong that it also remembers earlier sessions on its own. |

**Summary:** Riley has the shape of the loop, knows it needs a stopping condition, and knows tools are chosen from their descriptions. Two ideas need fixing. First, the model only outputs text; the program runs the tools and calls the model again after each result, which also decides the call count and cost. Second, the model has no memory of its own between sessions. M3 is the "automatic memory" distractor on q1, which Riley didn't pick. I used it for q6 because that is where the belief showed.

**Next step:** Riley re-traces the laser cutter request on paper. They label each step "model output" or "program action" and count the model calls. That sets up the memory lesson, where the program saves information and puts it back into the model's input.

I also wrote learning record `0003-who-runs-the-tools-and-who-remembers.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s2.json` (the retake from memory) is still ungraded. Do you want me to grade it next?
